definition: Lasting for a very short time.
example: The morning fog was ephemeral, gone before the first coffee.

definition: Present, appearing, or found everywhere.
example: Coffee shops are ubiquitous in this part of town.

definition: Using very few words.
example: His laconic reply was simply: "Done."

definition: The occurrence of happy or beneficial events by chance.
example: Finding the bookshop in the rain was pure serendipity.

definition: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically.
example: She took a pragmatic approach and shipped the simplest version first.

definition: A subtle difference in meaning, expression, or sound.
example: The translation missed every nuance of the original poem.

definition: Able to recover quickly from difficulty.
example: The team proved resilient after a rough quarter.

definition: The quality of being open and honest.
example: I appreciated the candor in her feedback.

definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
example: He kept meticulous notes on every experiment.

definition: Extremely idealistic and unrealistic in a charming way.
example: Rebuilding the whole system in a weekend was a quixotic plan.

definition: Fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing.
example: Her eloquent closing argument won the room.

definition: Holding firmly to something; persistent.
example: A tenacious bug survived three rewrites.

definition: Understood by only a small number of people with special knowledge.
example: The talk drifted into esoteric details of compiler design.

definition: Fond of company; sociable.
example: The most gregarious person at the table knew everyone by name.

definition: To place two things close together for contrasting effect.
example: The design juxtaposes hard concrete with soft light.

definition: Overly concerned with minor details or rules.
example: It sounds pedantic, but the distinction actually matters here.

definition: Clear, logical, and convincing.
example: He made a cogent case for delaying the launch.

definition: Not harmful or offensive.
example: The change looked innocuous until it hit production.

definition: Brisk and cheerful readiness.
example: She accepted the assignment with alacrity.

definition: Stated or appearing to be true, but not necessarily so.
example: The ostensible reason for the meeting was a status update.

definition: Countless or extremely great in number.
example: There are myriad ways to solve it; only two are cheap.

definition: Having knowledge of events before they happen.
example: His prescient warning about the outage went unread.

definition: To make something unclear or hard to understand.
example: The report seemed written to obfuscate the real numbers.

definition: Most noticeable or important.
example: Give me the three salient points before the call.

definition: Experienced through the feelings or actions of another person.
example: I get vicarious satisfaction from watching him finish a marathon.

definition: Open and responsive to suggestion; easily persuaded.
example: The client was amenable to a smaller first release.

definition: A feeling of fear or agitation about something that may happen.
example: She opened the deploy log with some trepidation.

definition: Using more words than needed.
example: The docs are thorough but verbose.

definition: Having sharp judgment; shrewd.
example: An astute observation saved us a week of work.

definition: To charm or enchant, sometimes deceptively.
example: The demo beguiled the audience into ignoring the caveats.

definition: Involving strenuous effort; difficult and tiring.
example: Migrating the database was an arduous two-day job.

definition: Truthful and straightforward; frank.
example: Let me be candid about the timeline.

definition: Showing care and conscientiousness in one's work.
example: Diligent review caught the off-by-one error.

definition: A person or thing that is mysterious or hard to understand.
example: The intermittent failure remained an enigma for months.

definition: Very attentive to accuracy and detail; hard to please.
example: He is fastidious about naming things well.

definition: Relevant to a subject under consideration.
example: That history is interesting but not germane to the decision.

definition: A sign that something is about to happen.
example: Rising latency was the harbinger of a bigger failure.

definition: The force or energy that makes something happen.
example: The outage gave fresh impetus to the rewrite.

definition: Showing good judgment; sensible.
example: A judicious use of caching solved it.

definition: To arouse or inspire a feeling; to set alight.
example: One good class kindled a lifelong interest.

definition: Expressed clearly; easy to understand.
example: Her explanation was the most lucid I'd heard.

definition: Generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival.
example: He was magnanimous in defeat.

definition: Vague or ill-defined.
example: The requirements are still nebulous.

definition: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course.
example: The obstinate cache refused to invalidate.

definition: To make someone less angry or hostile.
example: A status page update placated most users.

definition: To put an end to; to subdue.
example: The demo quelled any doubts about feasibility.

definition: Not revealing one's thoughts readily; reserved.
example: He was reticent about why he left.

definition: Having keen judgment and discernment; wise.
example: A sagacious mentor saves you years.

definition: Saying little; reserved in speech.
example: The taciturn engineer spoke once, and everyone listened.

definition: Not restricted or restrained.
example: Give the prototype unfettered access to a test database only.

definition: To regard with great respect.
example: The community venerates the original maintainer.

definition: Feeling caution about possible dangers or problems.
example: Be wary of benchmarks you didn't run yourself.

definition: Showing great energy or enthusiasm for a cause.
example: A zealous reviewer left ninety comments.

definition: Clever or skillful in using the hands or mind.
example: An adroit refactor removed half the code.

definition: To support or strengthen.
example: New tests bolster confidence in the release.

definition: Careful to consider all circumstances and consequences.
example: Be circumspect before granting production access.

definition: A scarcity or lack of something.
example: There is no dearth of opinions on tabs versus spaces.

definition: Calmness and composure, especially in a difficult situation.
example: She handled the incident with remarkable equanimity.

definition: Attempting to avoid notice; secretive.
example: He took a furtive glance at the clock.

definition: To shock or excite someone into taking action.
example: The deadline galvanized the whole team.

definition: Overused and therefore lacking impact.
example: The slogan felt hackneyed by the third slide.
